The EU will ban social networks for under 13 and personal accounts for under 15

Ursula von der Leyen announced the framework of the future EU Kids Act in Strasbourg on September 16 in a speech about the state of the Union. The formal text will be presented by the Commission on Thursday together with Henna Virkkunen, Vice President for Technological Sovereignty.

The scheme is strict and gradual.
Under 13 years old, social networks are off-limits.
From 13 to 15, only "mini-accounts" are allowed: created and managed by parents, with limited features and time restrictions.

From 15 to 18, teenagers can create their own profile, but the platform must maintain a safe design: without addictive features, with enhanced settings.

Von der Leyen summarized it succinctly: "No social networks until 13. No personal account until 15." And separately: "Each age group has its own vulnerability. Therefore, each will have its own level of protection."

The essence of the law is not in another clause in the user agreement. Currently, a child can simply enter a fake birthdate and proceed. The Kids Act should make age verification a mandated obligation, not just a declaration. Brussels looked at Australia, which was the first to introduce a lower limit.
The logic of responsibility is also changing. "Platforms must prove that they are safe," said von der Leyen. "It's not about minors accessing social networks. It's about when and how we allow social networks to reach minors."

In the same speech, she listed what Europe is "not obliged to accept": features tailored to induce dependence; feeds that draw users into increasingly harsh content; photos of girls that AI turns into sexualized images. According to her, children in the EU spend four to six hours a day on screens. She called this "the capture of attention, focus, and consciousness" and "the theft of childhood."

Drafts that agencies saw before the speech go beyond social networks. Video platforms, online games, and AI chatbots could also fall under the same age ladder. The project discusses penalties for violators of up to 6% of global revenue. Until 18 years old, they want to remove autoplay, rewards for reposts, personal recommendations, and free messages from strangers on children's accounts.

This is not yet law. The text will go to the European Parliament and to the 27 capitals. France pushed for a minimum age of 15, Spain spoke of 16, the Commission's expert panel leaned towards 13. The compromise announced today falls right in the middle: complete shield until 13, a parental corridor until 15, "safe design" until adulthood.

If the text passes close to what was announced, TikTok, Instagram, YouTube, and others will no longer be able to dismiss it with the phrase "the user stated the age themselves."

📌 Token Vesting: Why Team and Investor Tokens Unlock Over Time

Main Points
⏺ Token vesting schedules control when founders, teams, and investors can claim their tokens
⏺ Unlocks are usually spread over months or years with cliffs and linear releases
⏺ This post explains how vesting protects projects from instant dump pressure

1️⃣ What Is Vesting — tokens reserved for insiders are locked and only become claimable at set dates
2️⃣ Cliff Period — an initial lockup (for example, 6–12 months) where no tokens unlock at all
3️⃣ Linear Unlock — after the cliff, tokens are released gradually, such as monthly over several years
4️⃣ Market Impact — large unlocks can increase sell pressure, so traders often track vesting calendars
5️⃣ Trust Signal — transparent vesting shows that core contributors are aligned for the long term, not just a quick exit

Final Thoughts

Token vesting turns insider allocations into a time-based commitment — the longer they’re locked in, the more skin in the game the project really has.

📊 PayPay has added UnionPay QR payments across participating Japanese merchants while SMBC has begun deploying an OpenAI-powered interpreter to bank employees. The two companies have not announced a partnership between the products. PayPay’s expansion concerns payments made by overseas visitors, while SMBC’s application handles spoken communication between bank employees and customers.

📣 Travelers can register UnionPay cards issued in mainland China, Hong Kong or Macau within the UnionPay App. At participating PayPay merchants, they can scan or present a payment code to complete purchases through the HIVEX network. PayPay said the service can be used for purchases such as meals, accommodations and souvenirs. Prices appear in Japanese yen at the merchant, while the customer’s application calculates the amount in their home currency.

❗️ HIVEX connects domestic merchants to overseas mobile-payment services without requiring separate technical integration for every wallet. TBCASoft, which operates the platform, said UnionPay App payments became available at HIVEX-enabled PayPay locations in early September. TBCASoft described the service as reaching more than 500 million linked UnionPay card users. The figure represents cards linked across UnionPay’s issuing network, not confirmed users of PayPay merchants in Japan.

The Bypass Breaks

Saudi Arabia built the East-West Pipeline to bypass the Strait of Hormuz. A drone strike turned the bypass itself into the bottleneck.

The 1,200-kilometer line moves crude from Saudi Arabia’s eastern fields to Yanbu on the Red Sea. After the September 10 attack, Riyadh shut it down and Yanbu halted loadings. 

Saudi Aramco has canceled or postponed late-September cargoes for European refiners, while market sources expect further delays into October and possibly November. 

No Saudi crude has left Yanbu since September 11, according to Vortexa shipping data cited by Argus.

Two regional officials told the Associated Press that repairs to a major pumping facility could take three to five weeks. One said the pipeline might resume partial flows during repairs but could not estimate the volume. 

Reuters’ industry sources put the range between a partial restart within days and repairs lasting five to six weeks.

U.S. Energy Secretary Chris Wright chose the optimistic end of that range. On September 15, he said crude should be moving through the pipeline “within days.” 

Satellite images show fire damage and blackened ground around pumping stations on the route. Riyadh has not released a full damage assessment.

Iranian channels call it total destruction. Washington calls it a matter of days. The oil buyers have already received the only forecast that matters: canceled cargoes.
